proposals.observation: Six sessions hit the quiz in 48 hours. Five of them loaded the intro and went nowhere. One reached the email-capture step and still did not complete. Completion rate is 0%. The intro step is the entire problem right now — people are arriving (from Instagram and direct, so intent exists) and bouncing before they answer question one. The intro copy or load experience is failing to make the next tap feel worth it.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro copy so it names the specific cost of not knowing your money script rather than selling the quiz as a product. The current text almost certainly opens with a promise about what the quiz gives you. That framing asks someone to trust a cold mechanism. Instead, name something they already feel — the tab they don't open, the savings account they stopped checking — so they recognise themselves before they've answered anything. Keep it to three sentences maximum. No headline that sounds like a quiz headline.
proposals.current_text: Discover your money personality and get a personalised plan to finally take control of your finances.
proposals.new_text: You probably earn enough. The question is why the number in your account never quite matches that. Four questions. Honest result. No fluff.

proposals.impact: replicate 66% open rate pattern across lower-performing sequences
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate on 12 sends. Money Avoidance is at 52.63% on 19 sends. Money Worship is at 37.5% on 16 sends. That gap between Vigilance and Worship is 29 percentage points, which on a small list is not noise — it is a subject-line and preview-text signal. The Vigilance sequence is doing something the other two are not, and the most likely explanation is that its subject line names a feeling the reader is already having rather than naming what the email will explain to them.
proposals.proposal: Open the Money Worship sequence's first email and audit its subject line and preview text against the Money Vigilance sequence's equivalents. Rewrite the Money Worship subject line so it names a specific, quiet internal experience a money-worship-leaning person has — not what money worship is, but what it feels like at 11pm when the thing they bought last month still hasn't made them feel steadier. One subject line edit, one preview text edit.
proposals.current_text:
Subject: Do you believe more money would solve everything?
Preview: Understanding money worship and what it means for you.
proposals.new_text:
Subject: The number keeps going up. The feeling doesn't.
Preview: Why hitting the next income target rarely lands the way you expected it to.

proposals.observation: Two workflow runs failed in the last 24 hours: Weekly Queue Topup at 18:55 UTC and Funnel-Hack Digest at 10:56 UTC. The content queue has exactly one post queued against 47 published. If Weekly Queue Topup is broken, the queue will hit zero within days and scheduled posts will stop. This is the most operationally urgent item in the data — a silent failure with a concrete deadline.
proposals.proposal: Open the Weekly Queue Topup workflow file and read its last failure log to identify whether the failure is an authentication error, a missing secret, or a changed API response shape. The fix is a single targeted correction — do not refactor the whole file. The blocked-paths rule covers .github/workflows/* so Joel must make this edit directly rather than via Fred's automated diff, but the diagnosis should be specific enough that it takes under ten minutes to act on.
proposals.new_text:
